{{Short description|German chemist (1935–2018)}}
[[Image:Stephan Tanneberger (2010).jpg|thumb|Stephan Tanneberger, 2010]]

'''Stephan Tanneberger''' (December 27, 1935 – March 5, 2018) was a German [[Oncology|oncologist]] and [[chemist]] who held leading positions in [[cancer research]] and therapy in the [[German Democratic Republic]] (GDR), serving as director of the ''Zentralinstitut für Krebsforschung'' (Central Institute of Cancer Research) of the ''[[Akademie der Wissenschaften der DDR]]'' (Academy of Sciences of the German Democratic Republic) from 1974 until 1990. He left Germany in 1991 to work in the field of palliative care for cancer patients in [[Italy]] as well as in various countries in the [[Third World]]. In 2005, he founded a Center for Peace Work in [[Anklam]] in northeast Germany.

==Career==
Stephan Tanneberger was born in 1935 in [[Chemnitz]]<ref name="Hartkopf1992">*  ''Tannenberger, Stephan.'' Biographical entry in: Werner Hartkopf: ''Die Berliner Akademie der Wissenschaften: Ihre Mitglieder und Preisträger 1700–1990.'' Akademie-Verlag, Berlin 1992, {{ISBN|3-05-002153-5}}, p.&nbsp;357</ref> and enrolled in [[medicine]] and [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Leipzig]] in 1954, where he obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1961<ref name="PhD1961">Tanneberger, Stephan: ''Studien zur Lävansynthese.'' Universität Leipzig, Mathematisch-naturwissenschaftliche Fakultät, Dissertation vom 19. Dezember 1961 ([http://d-nb.info/481074058 Entry] in the catalogue of the [[German National Library]])</ref> and his [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.]] in 1964<ref name="MD1964">Tanneberger, Stephan: ''Probleme der Anwendung der Zell- und Gewebezüchtung in der medizinischen Forschung: Differenzierung und Entdifferenzierung tierischer Zellen bei der Kultivierung in vitro.'' Universität Leipzig, Medizinische Fakultät, Dissertation vom 29. August 1964 ([http://d-nb.info/482389311 Entry] in the catalogue of the [[German National Library]])</ref> as well as his [[Habilitation]] in 1970.<ref name="Habil1970">Tanneberger, Stephan: ''Über In vitro Kulturen menschlicher Tumoren und deren Benutzung für Planung und Kontrolle der Chemotherapie maligner Erkrankungen.'' Universität Leipzig, Bereich Medizin, Habilitationsschrift vom 29. Januar 1970 ([http://d-nb.info/482010649 Entry] in the catalogue of the [[German National Library]])</ref> In 1971, he took up a position as senior physician at the ''Zentralinstitut für Krebsforschung'' of the ''Akademie der Wissenschaften der DDR'' in [[Buch (Berlin)|Berlin-Buch]] where he was promoted to chief physician in 1972 and to deputy director in 1973.<ref name="Hartkopf1992"/> Following the death of the institute's founding director Hans Gummel in May 1973, he was appointed Professor of Clinical and Experimental Cancer Biology by the Academy of Sciences and named director of the institute in 1974.<ref name="Hartkopf1992"/> He served in his position and led the national program for cancer research and control of the GDR until January 1990. From the beginning of 1989, he was also chairman of the ''Zentrum für Medizinische Wissenschaft'' (Center for Medical Sciences) of the Academy of Sciences<ref name="JB-AdW1989-p235">''Akademie der Wissenschaften der DDR. Jahrbuch 1989.'' Akademie-Verlag, Berlin 1989, p.&nbsp;235</ref> which coordinated the activities of all medical institutes of the academy.

After the [[German reunification]] in 1990, Tanneberger left Germany and worked as consultant for the [[World Health Organization]] in various third world countries, among them [[Bangladesh]], [[India]], [[North Korea]] and [[Albania]].<ref name="Fricker2008">Janet Fricker: ''A Reverence for Life in turbulent Times.'' In: ''Cancerworld.'' 27/2008. European School of Oncology, pp.&nbsp;26−32</ref> In 1993, he took up the position as head of quality control for ''Associazione Nazionale Tumori'' (ANT),<ref name="Fricker2008"/> an Italian organization which focuses on palliative care for cancer patients in their respective domestic environment as well as on [[Cancer#Prevention|cancer prevention]]. One year later, he became Secretary-General of ''ANT International'' and in 2000 scientific director of ''Instituto ANT''. Additionally, he is professor with teaching assignment at the [[University of Bologna]] since 1992.<ref name="Kurschner2003">''Tanneberger, Stephan.'' Biographical entry in: Bettina Bartz, Gerhard Lüdtke, Hans Strodel, Hans Jaeger: ''[[Kürschners Deutscher Gelehrten-Kalender]]. Bio-bibliographisches Verzeichnis deutschsprachiger Wissenschaftler der Gegenwart.'' Volume&nbsp;3. Saur, Munich 2003, {{ISBN|3-59-823607-7}}, p.&nbsp;3375</ref> He also directs a program of the [[European School of Oncology]] aimed at improving education and information exchange in the field of cancer control in [[Armenia]], [[Azerbaijan]], [[Moldova]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], [[Romania]] and [[Ukraine]] since 2005 and the ''Euro-Arab School of Oncology'' since 2008.

Tanneberger has published several books about his experience regarding treatment of cancer and care for terminally ill patients. In addition to his medical activities, he is also active in the field of peace work. In 2004, he launched the foundation ''Zentrum für Friedensarbeit - Otto Lilienthal - Hansestadt Anklam'' (Center for Peace Work) in Anklam in northeast Germany.<ref name="Fricker2008"/> Since then, he acts as chairman of the foundation's executive board and is involved with the restoration of a former [[Wehrmacht prison Anklam|Wehrmacht prison in Anklam]] as well as with the project ''Wald für Frieden und gegen Klimawandel'' (Forest for Peace and against Climate Change) which is part of the [[United Nations Billion Tree Campaign|Billion Tree Campaign]] of the [[United Nations Environment Programme]] (UNEP).

Tanneberger was married from 1970 until 2000 and is the father of a son and two daughters.<ref name="Fricker2008"/> He died of cancer in 2018.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nordkurier.de/anklam/stephan-tanneberger-ist-tot-0731439403.html | title=DDR-Krebsforscher und Friedensaktivist: Stephan Tanneberger ist tot &#124; Nordkurier.de | date=7 March 2018 }}</ref>

== Awards and distinctions ==

In recognition of his work, Tanneberger received numerous national and international awards and distinctions. In 1986, he was awarded the honorary title ''Verdienter Wissenschaftler des Volkes'' (Merited Scientist of the GDR).<ref name="JB-AdW1989-p191">''Tanneberger, Stephan MR Professor Dr. rer. nat. Dr. med. habil., geb. am 27.12.1935 in Chemnitz.'' Biographical entry in: ''Akademie der Wissenschaften der DDR. Jahrbuch 1989.'' Akademie-Verlag, Berlin 1989, p.&nbsp;191</ref> The Academy of Sciences of the GDR made him a corresponding member in 1981 and an ordinary member in 1989.<ref name="Hartkopf1992"/> In March 2012, he received the ''Sigillo d'argento'' (Silver Seal) of the University of Bologna.<ref name="Bologna2012">Matteo Benni: ''[http://www.magazine.unibo.it/Magazine/Notizie/2012/03/23/Il_sigillo_argento_Alma_Mater.htm Il sigillo d'argento dell'Alma Mater consegnato a Stephan Tanneberger]'' published by ''UniBo Magazine'' on March 23, 2012</ref>

* ''Cancer In Developing Countries: The Great Challenge For Oncology In The 21st Century.'' Munich, 2004
* ''Cancer Medicine At The Dawn Of The 21st Century.'' Bologna, 2006
* ''ESMO Handbook of Advanced Cancer Care.'' London and New York, 2006
